dispositions.finding_summary: A mutation's late completion (create/update/delete response released after the user switched workspaces) changed the NEW workspace's UI state and feedback: it closed the new form and dropped its unsaved input, reloaded the list, announced into the new workspace's live region, or raised the error banner. Terra's diagnostic confirmed the write itself stays in the originating workspace; the defect is the unscoped completion effects.
dispositions.disposition: fixed_in_baseline (unintended defect; the intentionally unguarded switch-time draft discard preserved)
dispositions.policy_choice: Scope discipline for in-flight action completion: every mutation handler captures the workspace scope at submit time via a selectedIdRef mirror (useRef kept in sync by an effect), and every completion effect — success/failure announcement, form close plus draft reset, list reload, error banner, delete-confirm reset — is skipped when the selection changed while the action was in flight. deleteItem owns its entire error path internally (so the row's onClick stays a plain void call and cannot double-handle errors). The write itself was and remains correctly scoped to the originating workspace; nothing about request routing changed.
changes: baseline/src/components/Workboard.tsx — selectedIdRef mirror; createItem/updateItem/deleteItem capture scope at submit and guard all completion effects on unchanged selection; row onClick simplified to a single owned call

baseline/docs/baseline-contract.md §6 — normative rule: a mutation's completion effects stay scoped to the workspace it started in; only the switch-time draft discard remains intentionally unguarded

dispositions.finding_summary: The unqualified 'unsupported methods → 404' wording contradicted observed behavior: Hono dispatches HEAD through the GET route (auth enforced, empty body), and Better Auth's catch-all answers unknown sub-routes on mounted methods with its own 404 (empty body), not the app envelope. The R1 test proved only one narrow case.
dispositions.disposition: fixed_in_baseline_docs_and_tests (documentation corrected to observed granularity; representative exception tests added)
dispositions.policy_choice: Route/method precedence is documented exactly as observed first-hand: (1) HEAD is not an unsupported method — it is served through the GET route, so the GET status applies (auth included) with an empty body (HEAD /api/health → 200 empty; unauthenticated HEAD /api/me → 401 empty; HEAD on an unknown path → 404 empty, no envelope body); (2) unknown paths and unsupported methods on known app routes return 404 not_found in the app envelope regardless of session state; (3) /api/auth/* is mounted for GET and POST only — on those methods Better Auth answers unknown sub-routes with its native 404 and an empty body (no app envelope), while other methods fall through to the app 404 envelope.
changes: baseline/docs/baseline-contract.md §5 — route/method precedence rewritten at the observed granularity (HEAD-via-GET, app-envelope cases, Better Auth native-404 cases)
docs/faq-draft.md Q13 — same correction, question-form wording

baseline/tests/api/auth.test.ts — extended: 'serves HEAD through the GET route with an empty body and enforced auth' (3 sub-cases); 'uses Better Auth's own 404 for unknown auth sub-routes on mounted methods' (GET/POST native empty-body 404; DELETE app envelope); '404s an unsupported method on a known path regardless of session state' (DELETE /api/health with and without a session cookie, both app-envelope 404)
dispositions.evidence: A disposable route probe (scratch .probe-routes.mts, removed after use) reproduced every documented behavior first-hand before the docs were written; the new tests encode those observations and pass (auth.test.ts 8 → 10 tests; api suite 34 → 36).
remaining_limitations: Behavior beyond the verified paths (other methods on Better Auth mounts, other sub-route shapes) remains documented as observed-for-these-cases only; FAQ keeps this as an open question.

dispositions.finding_summary: The UI was required to render date-difference labels ('3 days' vs '2 days' across a midnight) without reading a clock and without receiving the server's today or any offset, so the label was not derivable from the required response; the 'permanently past' seed date was future-or-today on early runs, and unpinned real-clock cases could cross calendar boundaries.
dispositions.disposition: fixed_in_contracts (S08 defines an explicit server-to-client time interface and a pinned deterministic test clock)
dispositions.policy_choice: Wire interface (additive, no silent extra fields): the items-list envelope gains a top-level today: "YYYY-MM-DD" (the server's day string for that request), and each item gains a dueState computed on the server by a pure shared helper with signature (dueDate: string | null, today: "YYYY-MM-DD") → dueState; the UI renders labels from (dueState, envelope today) through that shared helper and never reads a clock for due labels; a per-item today is deliberately not added, and single-item responses carry dueState while label rendering always uses fresh list data. Determinism: when the test-only environment variable WORKBOARD_FAKE_TODAY is set to a real calendar date in 2000–2099, the server uses it as today for dueState and the envelope today (created_at/updated_at keep the real clock); an invalid value makes the server fail fast at startup rather than being silently ignored; without the variable behavior is identical to wall-clock today. The e2e pin is 2026-11-07, and label cases (overdue/today/due-soon singular and plural/later boundary at N=7/8) are enumerated under that pin with explicit UTC/TZ boundary rules.
changes: contracts/S08-due-date-semantics.md — envelope today field, per-item dueState, shared pure helper, WORKBOARD_FAKE_TODAY semantics incl. fail-fast, pinned e2e day 2026-11-07, enumerated expected labels, migration permissions (see R1-N4)
dispositions.evidence: The pinned-day grammar examples were recomputed by hand and cross-checked against the contract's enumerated table; the fail-fast rule removes the silent-override failure mode Terra demonstrated; all label cases are now functions of (dueDate, envelope today) with no clock read.
remaining_limitations: The interface is unimplemented by design until an S08 task run; its task tests are the verifier.
WORKBOARD_FAKE_TODAY is test-only by contract; a task implementation that leaks it into created_at/updated_at would violate the stated rule (that check belongs to S08's acceptance).

dispositions.finding_summary: The unconditional 'no new items appear mid-walk' guarantee is unattainable for a two-field live keyset (same-millisecond create with an id sorting after the page-boundary cursor legitimately appears on a later page without any clock moving backwards), and the default-limit acceptance was off by one (at exactly 20 rows with limit 20 there is no next page, so nextCursor must be null, not non-null).
dispositions.disposition: fixed_in_contracts (S03 rewritten to an attainable consistency model; acceptance threshold corrected)
dispositions.policy_choice: Consistency model: a total order over (updatedAt, id) exists and is stable for existing items; existing items never repeat across pages and never change position relative to each other mid-walk; the single disclosed exception is an item CREATED during the walk whose updatedAt exactly equals a page-boundary timestamp and whose id sorts after that boundary's id — it can appear on a later page (attainable tie semantics instead of an unattainable exclusion; no clock movement is implied). Walk examples require a clock precondition that is observed, not assumed: the wi_108 bump-to-top example is exercised only when the observed server time exceeds the newest seed timestamp. Acceptance corrected: a workspace with exactly 20 items and default limit 20 returns 20 items with nextCursor: null; adding a 21st returns 20 items with a non-null cursor and the cursor walk yields the 21st with nothing repeating.
changes: contracts/S03-stable-cursor-pagination.md — revision marker R2; consistency model rewritten (total order, no-repeats with the disclosed same-millisecond tie exception, skip tolerance unchanged, observed-clock precondition for mutation examples); acceptance table row fixed to the exact-20/21 threshold
dispositions.evidence: Disposable SQLite keyset probe (scratch .probe-keyset.mts + probe.db, removed after use): reproduced Terra's page-1 boundary, inserted a same-millisecond larger-id row, and confirmed it appears on page 2 (tie exception is real, not hypothetical); confirmed exactly-20 → null and 21 → non-null cursor behavior against a limit-20 keyset. The first probe run contained a cursor-binding bug (bound values in the wrong order); it was corrected and the corrected probe's results are the ones cited.
remaining_limitations: Excluding new items entirely would require extra server state (e.g. a walk-start snapshot watermark); that remains a coordinator decision, disclosed as an alternative in the contract rather than implemented.
The tie exception's visibility depends on insert order within the same millisecond; task tests must seed explicit timestamps to exercise it deterministically.

dispositions.finding_summary: S04 simultaneously required the baseline create message for a missing title ('title is required.') and specified 'title must be a non-empty string.' for missing/empty title, so two reasonable implementations produced incompatible exact 422 payloads; non-object entries were forbidden but had no specified first-problem message or precedence against invalid fields.
dispositions.disposition: fixed_in_contracts (S04 reconciles the messages and specifies entry-level diagnostics and precedence)
dispositions.policy_choice: Exact message split: a MISSING title keeps the baseline create message 'title is required.'; a present-but-empty or non-string title yields 'title must be a non-empty string.' A non-object entry (null, array, scalar) yields the entry-level message 'entry <i>: entry must be a JSON object.' (422), and entry-level validation is checked BEFORE field-level checks, so a malformed entry never interleaves field diagnostics. Precedence within an entry follows the baseline create validator.
changes: contracts/S04-transactional-import.md — revision marker R2; message table rewritten with the missing/empty split, the entry-level message, and the entry-before-field precedence; worked examples added for both orders
dispositions.evidence: The reconciled messages were checked against the actual baseline validator text (server/api.ts create path) so the missing-title message is byte-identical to the baseline; examples in the contract now state the exact fields object for each malformed-input case.
remaining_limitations: Exact 422 payload equality is verified only when an S04 task implementation exists.

dispositions.finding_summary: S07's draft trigger ('save while values differ from pristine') and its public example (clear a typed title back to empty, then expect the empty values restored) could not both govern: once values return to pristine the trigger stops saving, so an earlier-saved draft could keep the stale typed title; the state of an already-saved draft after reversion was unspecified.
dispositions.disposition: fixed_in_contracts (S07 defines pristine-reversion semantics and fixes the trigger)
dispositions.policy_choice: The draft trigger is 'values changed while the form is open', not 'values differ from pristine': any change saves (debounced), including a change back to empty. Reversion to pristine is therefore a normal change: it re-fires the debounce and OVERWRITES the stored draft with the pristine values — a draft is never deleted by reversion, and no previously saved stale title can survive. Pending-debounce case: a reversion cancels/replace-pends nothing special — the last debounced write always reflects the latest values, so storage converges to the pristine values.
changes: contracts/S07-failure-safe-editing.md — revision marker R2; requirement 1 trigger reworded; pristine-reversion semantics specified (re-fire, overwrite, never delete); the public example now follows from the trigger
dispositions.evidence: The reworked state machine was walked by hand against Terra's exact example sequence (open create form → type title → clear to empty) for both debounce timings (fired before clear, and pending at clear); both converge to the empty draft being saved and restored.
remaining_limitations: Draft persistence internals (storage shape) remain baseline-defined; only the observable save/restore semantics are contractual.
